name: @dineug/erd-editor-mcp

tools.name: erd_list_documents
tools.description: Lists ERD documents with path, open, active, dirty and readonly. With an editor serving the working directory (the VS Code extension, the Obsidian plugin or the JetBrains IDE plugin) it lists that editor's, every open project's in a JetBrains IDE; otherwise the ERD files under the working directory.

tools.name: erd_open_document
tools.description: Opens a document for editing, in the ERD editor of the editor that serves it, if one does (the VS Code extension, the Obsidian plugin or the JetBrains IDE plugin). With create it makes the file first if missing; a name with no extension gets .erd.json.

path.description: Path of the ERD document (.erd.json, .erd, .vuerd), absolute or relative to the working directory.

create.description: True to create an empty document when the file does not exist.

tools.name: erd_save
tools.description: Saves a document an editor holds to disk. VS Code keeps edits unsaved until this is called; Obsidian and JetBrains IDEs save them as they save the user’s edits, and this writes them at once. On disk, with no editor, edits are written at once and this does nothing.

path.description: Path of the ERD document (.erd.json, .erd, .vuerd), absolute or relative to the working directory.

tools.name: erd_undo
tools.description: Reverts the last edit this agent made to the document, never the user’s edits. Calls that made no undo entry are skipped and named.

path.description: Path of the ERD document (.erd.json, .erd, .vuerd), absolute or relative to the working directory.

tools.name: erd_redo
tools.description: Applies again the edit erd_undo last reverted.

path.description: Path of the ERD document (.erd.json, .erd, .vuerd), absolute or relative to the working directory.

tools.name: erd_read
tools.description: Reads a document as a snapshot, as DDL, as its raw JSON or, with the scripts format, its before and after scripts alone. The sql format of the whole document includes the document's before and after scripts. The sql format with tableIds, tableNames or groupNames gives the DDL of just those tables, the way to read a large schema; a read too large for one answer is refused with how to narrow it. For ids and details prefer erd_list and erd_get. Change a document only through the erd_ tools, never by writing its file.

path.description: Path of the ERD document (.erd.json, .erd, .vuerd), absolute or relative to the working directory.

format.description: snapshot: compact JSON with every id, column and table group, large on a big schema. sql: DDL of a vendor. json: the whole raw .erd.json document, larger still; never write this into the file. scripts: just the document's before and after scripts, as JSON { before, after }, each empty when unset, whatever the size of the schema.

vendor.description: Database for the sql format; defaults to the database the document is set to.

statements.description: For the sql format: create (default), ifNotExists, which writes CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS on MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite and Databricks and falls back to create elsewhere, or recreate, which drops the tables first (Snowflake writes CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE).

header.description: For the sql format: none (default), use, which selects the database or schema the document's database name gives, or createAndUse, which creates it first. Oracle has use alone, so createAndUse writes use there; PostgreSQL has createAndUse alone, so use writes no header there; SQLite has neither and writes none. No header is written while the database name is empty or not a plain identifier.

tableIds.description: For the sql format: the DDL of these tables only, with the foreign keys they hold, which name the tables they reference.

tableNames.description: For the sql format: tables by name, in any case, as tableIds takes them by id.

groupNames.description: For the sql format: the tables of these table groups, by group name in any case, joined with tableIds and tableNames.

tools.name: erd_list
tools.description: Lists a document: its settings and counts, then a page of tables, each with its id, position and size on the ERD canvas (the width approximate, the height exact), with their indexes and relationships (each relationship once, with one of its tables) and, for a table in a table group, its groupId; after the tables come the table groups, then the memos. A small schema fits in one page. On a larger one, nextOffset and note say how to go on: query finds tables by a word, namesOnly lists every table name in a call or a few. Columns, comments, memo text and the tables of a group come from erd_get; the foreign keys a table holds, from erd_read sql with tableNames.

path.description: Path of the ERD document (.erd.json, .erd, .vuerd), absolute or relative to the working directory.

query.description: Words to look for inside table names and comments and column names and comments, in any case; tables whose names hold more of the words come first.

offset.description: Where the page starts in the list, 0 by default; pass the nextOffset of the page before, with the same query.

limit.description: At most this many entries in the page, 100 by default and no limit with namesOnly; a page also stops where one answer is full.

namesOnly.description: True for the table names alone, as many as one answer holds; erd_get and erd_read take tableNames.

tools.name: erd_get
tools.description: Gives the entities named, in full: tables with their columns and size, relationships with their columns, indexes with their columns, memos with their text, table groups with their tables. Ids and names that name nothing live are listed in missing; ids one answer has no room for are listed in notReturned, to ask for again.

path.description: Path of the ERD document (.erd.json, .erd, .vuerd), absolute or relative to the working directory.

tableNames.description: Table names, in any case, from erd_list; a name gives every table so named.

tools.name: erd_add_relationship
tools.description: Relates two tables: copies the parent primary key into the child as foreign key columns, creating an unnamed primary key column first if the parent has none (its foreign key column is unnamed too). Each foreign key column is named from its key: a key of one word, only letters and digits with no camelCase break and no switch between cased letters and caseless ones such as Hangul or kana (id, ID, uuid, id2), gets the parent table and an underscore in front (users_id for the key id of users), any other key (member_id, userId, UserID, 회원ID, _id, order-no) or one equal to the table name stays as it is, and a name the child already has is numbered (users_id_2). Each foreign key column copies the data type of its key, but a serial key gives the integer it stores: serial4 integer, smallserial and serial2 smallint, bigserial and serial8 bigint, and a bare serial integer under PostgreSQL, bigint unsigned under MySQL and MariaDB and serial elsewhere, written in capitals when the type of the key is. Name the parent table first: an unnamed parent gives the key name alone (id), and a later rename leaves these names as they are. createdIds holds, in order, that new parent key column if one was made, the foreign key columns, then the relationship id last.

path.description: Path of the ERD document (.erd.json, .erd, .vuerd), absolute or relative to the working directory.

startTableId.description: Parent table id, the referenced side that holds the primary key.

endTableId.description: Child table id, which receives the foreign key columns.

relationshipType.description: Cardinality at the child end: ZeroOne (0..1), ZeroN (0..N), OneOnly (exactly 1) or OneN (1..N).

onDelete.description: What the database does to the child rows: none (no clause, the database default), noAction, cascade, setNull, setDefault or restrict. A vendor that lacks the action drops it from its DDL. An ERD Editor extension or plugin released before referential actions ignores this setting, so the user should update it.

onUpdate.description: What the database does to the child rows: none (no clause, the database default), noAction, cascade, setNull, setDefault or restrict. A vendor that lacks the action drops it from its DDL. An ERD Editor extension or plugin released before referential actions ignores this setting, so the user should update it.

endTableId.description: Child table id, the side holding the foreign key.

endColumnIds.description: Foreign key column ids in the child table, one per start column, in the same order.

relationshipType.description: Cardinality at the child end: ZeroOne (0..1), ZeroN (0..N), OneOnly (exactly 1) or OneN (1..N).

onDelete.description: What the database does to the child rows: none (no clause, the database default), noAction, cascade, setNull, setDefault or restrict. tools.name: erd_add_table_group

Pass tableIds to wrap those tables, each leaving any group it was in, or a rect (x, y, width and height), which takes in every table in no group whose centre lies inside it, as drawing a group in the editor does. A table is in one group at most. An ERD Editor extension or plugin released before table groups ignores this edit and drops every group when it saves, so the user should update it.

tools.name: erd_set_table_group
tools.description: Puts tables in a table group, each leaving any group it was in, or with groupId null takes them out of their groups. Tables already where they go are left alone. An ERD Editor extension or plugin released before table groups ignores this edit and drops every group when it saves, so the user should update it.

path.description: Path of the ERD document (.erd.json, .erd, .vuerd), absolute or relative to the working directory.

groupId.description: Table group id to put the tables in, from erd_list; null or an empty string takes them out of every group.

tools.name: erd_set_database_name
tools.description: Sets the database name of the document. erd_undo cannot revert it: the editor keeps no undo entry for this setting.

path.description: Path of the ERD document (.erd.json, .erd, .vuerd), absolute or relative to the working directory.

value.description: The database name.

tools.name: erd_set_database
tools.description: Sets the database vendor, which picks the data types and the default DDL of erd_read sql. erd_undo cannot revert it: the editor keeps no undo entry for this setting.

path.description: Path of the ERD document (.erd.json, .erd, .vuerd), absolute or relative to the working directory.

value.description: The database vendor.

tools.name: erd_set_ddl_script
tools.description: Sets one of the two SQL scripts the document keeps for its Schema SQL: before, written ahead of the tables, such as CREATE EXTENSION or CREATE SCHEMA, or after, written past the generated DDL, such as GRANT or CREATE VIEW. It replaces the whole script, so read the current one first with erd_read format scripts. The text goes as is into the DDL of every database, so write it for the document's database; SQL Server output gets GO after a script that does not end with GO. An empty string removes it. erd_read sql shows it in place. An ERD Editor extension or plugin released before scripts neither shows nor keeps them, so the user should update it.

path.description: Path of the ERD document (.erd.json, .erd, .vuerd), absolute or relative to the working directory.

position.description: before or after the generated tables.

sql.description: The script, at most 10,000 characters; an empty string removes it.

tools.name: erd_import_sql
tools.description: Replaces every table, relationship, index, memo and table group of the document with the schema parsed from SQL DDL (CREATE TABLE statements), keeping its settings but the view, which goes to the start of the canvas; erd_undo restores what it replaced. With mode append it instead adds the schema's tables, relationships and indexes as new ones in a grid below the diagram, leaving every table and setting already there as it is; a foreign key to a table the text does not declare is dropped.

path.description: Path of the ERD document (.erd.json, .erd, .vuerd), absolute or relative to the working directory.

value.description: The SQL DDL (CREATE TABLE statements) source text.

mode.description: replace, the default, loads the import in place of every table, relationship, index, memo and table group and keeps the settings but the view, which goes to the start of the canvas; append adds what the import holds as new tables below the diagram and keeps everything already there, a table of the same name included.

tools.description: Replaces every table, relationship, index, memo and table group of the document with the schema parsed from DBML, keeping its settings but the view, which goes to the start of the canvas; erd_undo restores what it replaced. With mode append it instead adds the schema's tables, relationships and indexes as new ones in a grid below the diagram, leaving every table and setting already there as it is; a foreign key to a table the text does not declare is dropped. tools.name: erd_import_json
tools.description: Replaces the whole document, its settings included, with an erd-editor JSON document such as another .erd.json file: the settings and locks it holds take the place of this document's, and one without lockSettings turns every lock on and puts the view at the start of the canvas. To keep this document's settings, start from the text erd_read json gives. erd_undo restores the previous document. With mode append it instead adds that document's tables, relationships, indexes, memos and table groups as new ones below the diagram, apart as the file places them, and keeps this document's settings. An ERD Editor extension or plugin released before table groups drops every group when it saves, so the user should update it.

path.description: Path of the ERD document (.erd.json, .erd, .vuerd), absolute or relative to the working directory.

value.description: The .erd.json document text; empty gives an empty document, and is refused with mode append.

mode.description: replace, the default, loads the document in place of this one, its settings included; append adds its tables, relationships, indexes, memos and table groups below the diagram and keeps everything already there, a table of the same name included.

tools.name: erd_batch
tools.description: Runs several edit tools in order as one edit, all or none: they are tried on a copy first, so a refusal names the operation and leaves the document as it was. One erd_undo reverts the whole batch. Name an operation with as, then pass $name for its first created id, $name.1 for its second or $name.last for its last, where a later operation takes an entity id.

path.description: Path of the ERD document (.erd.json, .erd, .vuerd), absolute or relative to the working directory.

tool.description: An erd_ edit tool, such as erd_add_column.

as.description: A name for the ids this operation creates, which a later operation passes as $name, $name.1 or $name.last.

args.description: The tool arguments without path; where one takes an entity id, $name refers to an earlier operation.

operations.description: The edit tool calls to run, at most 100, each { tool, as, args }.

instructions: Edits erd-editor ERD documents (.erd.json) one operation per tool. Find ids with erd_list, which also gives each table its position and size, and read columns and other details with erd_get; then pass the ids to the edit tools, several at once with erd_batch, such as a table with its columns. On a schema of hundreds or thousands of tables erd_list answers a page at a time: find the tables a task needs with its query or namesOnly, then read just those with erd_get or erd_read sql. Never write a document file yourself. When an editor serves the document (the ERD Editor extension in VS Code, or its plugin in Obsidian or a JetBrains IDE), edits appear live in its ERD editor: VS Code keeps them unsaved until erd_save, while Obsidian and JetBrains IDEs save them as they save the user’s edits and erd_save writes them at once. Otherwise they are written to the file at once.
